situations.name: Metric tile
situations.definition: A developer needs a single labeled figure with an icon, optional trend and sparkline, rendered consistently across a dashboard.
situations.note: KpiTile explicitly consolidated 3 hand-rolls and reached 10 call sites, but 7 more private Stat/Tile/MiniStat/StatTile shapes plus 2 home-cockpit widgets grew back around it — its 3 densities never covered the clickable-filter tile or the config-driven widget.

situations.name: Summary count strip
situations.definition: A developer needs the header row of aggregate counts above a list, and must decide whether each count reflects the server total or only the loaded page.
situations.note: Five surfaces compute the same strip five ways (backend summary struct, server L0 counts, client reduce over the page, pure model fn, store field); the honest count usually lives server-side while the visible one is page-local, and a comment at DashboardHomeMissionControl.tsx:102 records a pagination hint already having been mistaken for a row total.

situations.name: Chart card frame
situations.definition: A developer needs the card shell around a chart — title, icon chip, height, actions slot, empty branch, error boundary — before writing any chart.
situations.note: Three competing shells exist simultaneously (MetricChart, DashboardChartCard, and a fully inline div+ChartErrorBoundary+LazyChart repeated 4x in one file); DashboardChartCard's own docstring promises to absorb the others but the migration stopped at stage 1.

situations.name: Lazy chart loading
situations.definition: A developer needs Recharts to load off the critical path and to fail without taking the page down.
situations.note: The one genuinely settled piece of the charting stack — every chart site goes through LazyChart's render-prop and ChartErrorBoundary, including the hand-rolled frames.

situations.name: Sparkline
situations.definition: A developer needs a tiny inline trend line next to a figure, with no charting library.
situations.note: The divergence is semantic, not cosmetic: KpiTile normalizes to the sample's own min/max while directorScore deliberately anchors to a fixed 0-5 so scores stay comparable across rows — two opposite correct answers with no shared vocabulary for choosing.

situations.name: Proportional bar
situations.definition: A developer needs a horizontal bar whose fill encodes a ratio — utilization, share of total, progress, score.
situations.note: The single worst divergence in the slice: 33 files hand-roll `style={{ width: `${pct}%` }}` with no shared primitive, each re-deciding three independent axes — normalization (absolute vs share-of-max vs share-of-total), the min-visible floor (2%, 4%, 8%, none), and whether the tint comes from the value or from a sibling field (BurnBar tints by budgetRatio but sizes by burn rate).

situations.name: Trend delta indicator
situations.definition: A developer needs an up/down arrow plus percentage next to a metric, and must decide which direction is 'good'.
situations.note: A shared TrendIndicator exists with an `invertPolarity` prop, yet KpiTile reimplemented identical logic inline with a differently-named `invertColor`; every other site hardcodes green-up/red-down, which is simply wrong for cost, latency and error-rate tiles.

situations.name: Period-over-period comparison
situations.definition: A developer needs 'vs. previous period' deltas from a time series and must not invent one when no prior period was fetched.
situations.note: computeTrends is the canonical answer and its docstring records the bug it killed (a front-half/back-half heuristic that 'used to lie on the Home Runs tile'), but useNavCardStatus still hand-rolls pctChange with a prev===0 => 100% rule that computeTrends deliberately suppresses for averages.

situations.name: Rate metric identity
situations.definition: A developer needs to render a percentage (success rate, uptime) and must pin down which numerator, denominator, source and time window it means.
situations.note: Only 3 identities are registered and only Mission Control consults the registry — every other percentage in the slice is computed inline, so the same label 'Success Rate' still means three different windows across tabs; the right shape, badly under-adopted.

situations.name: Weighted composite score
situations.definition: A developer needs to fold several signals into one 0-100 number with declared weights, and handle dimensions that have no data.
situations.note: compositeHealthScore is a model consolidation (dev-time sum-to-1.0 assertion, shared sub-score helpers so bar and score can't disagree) — but leaderboardScoring re-invents all of it, and Rust's classify_breach is a third independent health verdict with no shared constants; the file's own comment records 55% of the grade once being one metric double-counted.

situations.name: Grade and tier banding
situations.definition: A developer needs to convert a numeric score into a named band (A-F, elite/strong, high/mid/low) with a matching colour.
situations.note: GRADE_THRESHOLDS won inside sub_health after being duplicated verbatim three times, but thresholds keep getting re-inlined at render because a ternary is cheaper to write than an import — and the Rust breach classifier uses entirely different constants for the same verdict.

situations.name: Zero versus no-data
situations.definition: A developer must decide what to render when a metric has no samples at all, as distinct from a real measured zero.
situations.note: The most-commented recurring problem in the codebase and still mechanism-diverged: the null must survive the whole pipeline, because a single `?? 0` between SQL and JSX silently fabricates a perfect score and the failure is invisible — green means healthy AND means untested. Rust carries matching regression tests (p95_is_none_without_timed_executions).

situations.name: Data provenance disclosure
situations.definition: A developer needs to tell the user that a displayed number is stale, proxied, fleet-scoped, or cache-rescued rather than freshly measured.
situations.note: Six vocabularies for one idea (StalenessIndicator/fetchedAt, SuccessSourceBadge/measured-proxy-unknown, FleetTag/scope, useLiveRoadmap/fresh-cached-stale-unavailable, StalenessBanner/status-map) — and ObservabilityDashboard's own PanelStatusChips re-inlines the shared component's 300_000ms threshold instead of importing it.

situations.name: Token visual map
situations.definition: A developer needs to turn a machine token from Rust (status, severity, grade, event kind, category) into an icon, colour and translated label.
situations.note: The largest structural gap: 16+ hand-rolled class maps against a shared STATUS_PALETTE that roughly half the surfaces use. Each consumer needs a different slot subset (dot vs bar vs chip vs ring vs gradient stop) and SVG/canvas consumers need raw hex, which the shared token doesn't carry — sub_health alone holds two competing grade palettes.

situations.name: Severity taxonomy badge
situations.definition: A developer needs to rank, colour, shape and label an urgency level arriving from several different backend streams.
situations.note: Two incompatible token sets (critical/high/medium/low vs critical/warning/info) plus a third 'priority' vocabulary, reconciled by an inline bucketing at ReviewFocusFlow.tsx:269; one surface hand-draws SVG polygons for the colour-blind cue while another uses the shared StatusShape.

situations.name: Multi-condition status ladder
situations.definition: A developer needs a badge whose meaning depends on several fields evaluated in priority order, rendered at two or more densities.
situations.note: The exemplar worth codifying: it shares the circuit_breaker→auto_fix_pending→auto_fixed→severity branch LOGIC while parameterizing visual density via a `variant` prop — exactly the move the 16 other colour maps did not make. RotationOverviewPanel's 7-branch remediation ladder is the same shape, unshared.

situations.name: Relative timestamp
situations.definition: A developer needs to render 'how long ago' (or 'in how long') for a row, header or tooltip.
situations.note: Five implementations coexist because the shared answer is a component with hover-exact behaviour while half the call sites need a bare string to interpolate; StatusPageView and PersonaHealthDashboard carry byte-identical hand-rolled lastRefreshLabel memos.

situations.name: Number and cost formatting
situations.definition: A developer needs to render a count, currency, duration or percentage with locale-correct grouping and sensible compaction.
situations.note: Numeric reaches 38 files but 27 still call raw toFixed in JSX, and three near-identical ms formatters (formatMs, formatLatency, fmtMs) disagree on thresholds and units; the sub-problem only KpiTile solved is compaction-with-exact-value-on-hover so a large count never overflows.

situations.name: Percentile latency display
situations.definition: A developer needs to show p50/p95/p99 latency and distinguish 'no timed runs' from 'zero milliseconds'.
situations.note: Worst cross-boundary divergence found: THREE separate Rust percentile functions (sla.rs, metrics.rs, perf.rs) with different interpolation and different null semantics — one returns Option, one returns f64 — feeding five frontend surfaces that each re-derive their own ms formatter.

situations.name: Auto-refresh polling
situations.definition: A developer needs a surface to re-fetch on an interval without burning IPC while the tab is hidden or off-screen.
situations.note: Three answers compete and each solves a different half — usePolling (backoff + coordinator, 4 users), usePausableInterval (visibility + active gating, 1 user), and 9 bare setIntervals; useStatusPageData reimplements the shared hook from scratch because 'refresh immediately on tab-return' doesn't fit its enable/disable shape.

situations.name: Shared fetch spine
situations.definition: A developer needs several surfaces to read the same backend bundle without each issuing its own duplicate fetch.
situations.note: A real win — one pipeline fetch feeds Home, Observability and Mission Control with per-source error and fetchedAt maps; the residual hazard is the coupling comment at DashboardRangeSwitch.tsx:12 warning that a second range control would race the pipeline.

situations.name: Partial failure envelope
situations.definition: A developer needs a panel assembled from several independent fetches to stay useful when only some of them succeed.
situations.note: Rust actually has the better factoring (a typed HealthBundleErrors per source), while the frontend invents banner vs chip vs synthetic-fallback-row per surface — and one panel still uses Promise.all, so a single failed arm blanks both halves; useStatusPageData's comment records rejected arms previously vanishing silently.

situations.name: In-flight fetch supersession
situations.definition: A developer needs a late response from a superseded request not to overwrite the current view.
situations.note: Three mechanisms (closure `cancelled` flag x5, monotonic sequence token, AbortController) for one problem; Tauri IPC isn't abortable so the controller only guards application of the result — and useAnomalyDrilldown's comment records the exact bug: click A then B, A resolves last, user reads B's header with A's root cause.

situations.name: Cross-surface deep link
situations.definition: A developer needs one surface to open a specific row or tab in another, possibly not-yet-mounted, surface.
situations.note: Five idioms — module-level latch, storeBus event, context field, store field read-and-cleared, and a 4-setter imperative sequence — and incidents needs three at once because the target route is lazily mounted, a race its own header comment documents.

situations.name: Date range picker
situations.definition: A developer needs the day-window control that scopes a dashboard's queries.
situations.note: Three incompatible option vocabularies ([1,7,30,90] / [7,14,30,60,90] / fixed 365) and the divergence is partly CORRECT — each backend query has a different meaningful window, and the heatmap carries a comment explicitly forbidding unification; but the custom-range popover exists in only one, and every Rust command re-clamps independently.

situations.name: Dashboard filter scope
situations.definition: A developer needs persona and time-window filters shared across sibling tabs, and must keep clear which panes actually honour them.
situations.note: Cleanly split into values/actions contexts to avoid re-render storms, but the hard part is unsolved: Mission Control mixes persona-scoped and fleet-wide panes on one screen and hand-tags the fleet ones, because the per-persona aggregate query doesn't exist yet.

situations.name: Faceted filter bar
situations.definition: A developer needs the filter row above a list, ideally with a live count on each facet.
situations.note: The shared FilterBar has exactly one consumer among six; counts come from three different places and only some are truthful beyond the loaded page, which is why nobody trusts a single component.

situations.name: Narrowed filter detection
situations.definition: A developer needs to know whether the user has actually narrowed the view, to pick between 'all clear' and 'no matches'.
situations.note: A helper exists whose docstring claims three consumers, but one re-derives the check inline; getting it wrong is silently wrong rather than broken — the user sees the reassuring empty state instead of the corrective one.

situations.name: Empty state
situations.definition: A developer needs the block shown when a surface has nothing to display, distinguishing never-had-data from filtered-to-nothing from all-clear.
situations.note: Three competing families plus 7 more hand-rolls in health/observability alone, because in an observability context 'empty' is GOOD NEWS and needs a green-shield + show-all affordance, not a 'nothing here yet' illustration; the celebration branch also needs to know WHY the list drained, which only IncidentsInbox tracks.

situations.name: Ghost row placeholder
situations.definition: A developer needs a skeleton that mirrors a specific row or panel silhouette while the first page loads.
situations.note: Adjacent to the documented Page-loading law but worth separating: 15 bespoke skeletons cite the same doc yet share zero code, because the law itself demands content-shaped geometry. Only the health/ folder extracted the ghost-bar token; two files still use animate-pulse against the law.

situations.name: Decision queue
situations.definition: A developer needs a queue of pending items that a human resolves one at a time, advancing to the next on verdict.
situations.note: Converges at the write (resolveReviewRow, 4 call sites) but every surface hand-rolls its own state machine, because 'verdict' means 2-state approve/reject on one corpus, a 4-state lifecycle on another, and accept/reject/build-now on a third.

situations.name: Bulk selection actions
situations.definition: A developer needs multi-row selection with select-all and batched accept/reject/delete.
situations.note: A shared useToggleSet exists with ZERO consumers in this slice against three byte-identical hand-rolls; worse, execution semantics split — one uses Promise.allSettled with a partial-failure toast, another runs strictly sequentially because the store slice races.

situations.name: Per-item verdict map
situations.definition: A developer needs a review containing several sub-decisions, each individually accepted or rejected, plus accept-all.
situations.note: The backend stores one status per review, so per-item intent gets smuggled into a free-text notes field — and the 'Decisions:\n+ label\n- label' serializer is written twice independently, meaning the two writers can disagree on a format nothing validates.

situations.name: Master detail layout
situations.definition: A developer needs a list beside a detail pane, with a sensible mobile fallback.
situations.note: Four layouts (resizable splitter with its own RAF coalescer, fixed rail, modal-instead-of-pane, prose+margin-rail) and the mobile full-screen fallback exists in exactly one of them.

situations.name: Queue-walking detail modal
situations.definition: A developer needs prev/next navigation inside a detail modal over the list the user opened it from.
situations.note: The queue must be frozen at open time or a verdict re-sorts the list under the cursor — a rule three files independently rediscovered and commented; the shared nextQueueIndex helper covers two of five.

situations.name: Queue keyboard navigation
situations.definition: A developer needs j/k/arrow navigation and single-key verdicts over a queue, without colliding with other mounted surfaces.
situations.note: The same arrow keys legitimately mean 'verdict' on a deck and 'navigate' in a reader, and both can be mounted at once; a priority-claiming registry is the correct fix and only 2 of 7 adopted it — ReviewFocusFlow carries a comment about one keypress deciding two rows.

situations.name: Unread and seen state
situations.definition: A developer needs to mark items as seen and surface a count of what is new.
situations.note: Two incompatible data models — a durable per-row is_read column vs a lossy localStorage lastSeenAt watermark — and in the durable one both the list and the modal fire mark-as-read for the same click.

situations.name: Expandable disclosure row
situations.definition: A developer needs a row that expands into a detail panel, sometimes fetching its contents on expand.
situations.note: Eight re-implementations of useState(expanded) + chevron swap; only VitalsLedger supports more than one row open at a time, and three of them fetch on expand (one with a 30s ref-cache) — so the primitive would need a data-loading contract, not just visual state.

situations.name: Feed grouping and collapse
situations.definition: A developer needs a chronological or categorical feed bucketed into collapsible groups.
situations.note: 'Group' means a flat bucket list in two cases and a path-based tree in the others; the flat one needs sticky headers plus keyboard flattening, which the tree engine doesn't model, so neither can absorb the other.

situations.name: List pagination strategy
situations.definition: A developer needs to load more rows than fit in one query — infinite scroll, load-more, or a hard cap.
situations.note: Six strategies (keyset via shared hook, timestamp cursor, load-more button, hard limit + truncation banner, hasMore button, client page size) — the UI affordance is forced by the backing query shape, so this can only converge if the Rust query layer does first.

situations.name: View state persistence
situations.definition: A developer needs the user's filters, sort, collapse and column widths to survive navigation or restart.
situations.note: Four mechanisms — five separate localStorage keys each with its own try/catch and effect, server-side named saved_views, the shared useColumnWidths, and nothing at all — and the deliberate rule that some filters must NOT be restored exists in only one.

situations.name: Optimistic versus refetch write
situations.definition: A developer must choose whether a mutation updates the UI immediately or waits for a refetch, and how failure surfaces.
situations.note: The backend has three different failure semantics (throw, a boolean `false` refusal, compare-and-swap loss) and only one is expressible optimistically; ManualReviewList carries a comment recording that a missing catch once made failed verdicts look successful.

situations.name: Untyped payload normalization
situations.definition: A developer needs to render a free-form JSON/text blob whose shape varies by producer.
situations.note: A canonical parseDecisions exists and two of four consumers ignore it; the incidents variant must additionally handle three encodings (JSON, k=v, prose) with its own humanizeKey — each consumer needs a different slice of an untyped blob and picks its own.

situations.name: Alert rule editor
situations.definition: A developer needs a form defining metric, operator, threshold, severity and scope for a user-configurable alert.
situations.note: The UI converges on one form, but the rule LANGUAGE is implemented twice — alertSlice.evaluateRule in TS and evaluate_rule in Rust, kept in sync by a prose comment, with an already-documented deliberate divergence (server uses a 7-day cost_spike baseline, client used 1-day). Threshold units are metric-dependent so the form must hold strings until parse.

situations.name: Alert firing and dedupe
situations.definition: A developer needs fired alerts to respect a cooldown, not double-fire, surface as a toast, and land in history.
situations.note: TWO independent evaluation loops (a 60s UI loop and a Rust daemon) race on the same fired_alerts table and can double-fire inside the TTL window; the mitigation is a comment-documented handshake where the UI force-fetches history each tick, not a lock. Cooldown must be persisted to survive reload.

situations.name: Anomaly marker and drilldown
situations.definition: A developer needs statistical outliers marked on a chart and clickable through to a root-cause view.
situations.note: Frontend converges on one drilldown panel but the marker must be a chart-library primitive (a ReferenceLine with a custom SVG label render-prop, plus a reduced-motion branch) that no design-system component can wrap — and Rust holds FOUR separate anomaly detectors with different windows and thresholds.

situations.name: Chart annotation overlay
situations.definition: A developer needs deploy, rotation and incident markers overlaid on a time-series chart.
situations.note: A clean composer (merge/filter/sort/dedupe/cap over three IPC sources, debounced with AbortController); the subtlety is that annotation identity is fuzzy (date:type:label) and the sources tuple must stay referentially stable or it churns the memoized chart.

situations.name: Status page uptime strip
situations.definition: A developer needs a horizontal strip of day cells or segments summarising a window at a glance.
situations.note: One visual idiom encoding three different things (categorical day status, share-of-population, magnitude), so a shared component would need three value models; SLACard's comment records all its bars rendering at 0px before an explicit height was added. Day bucketing is backend and local-time-sensitive.

situations.name: Calendar heatmap
situations.definition: A developer needs a GitHub-style day-cell grid encoding activity intensity over a long window.
situations.note: Low recurrence, disproportionate difficulty: densifying a sparse response into a padded 53x7 grid is ~130 lines of date arithmetic, SVG rects can't host the shared Tooltip so it hand-rolls a portaled imperatively-positioned one, keyboard operability is built per cell, and it needs a bespoke Rust Mutex cache that exists nowhere else in the metrics repo.

situations.name: Ranked top-N bar list
situations.definition: A developer needs a leaderboard-style list where each row carries a bar proportional to some denominator.
situations.note: Eleven near-identical rank + name + value + bar rows, each re-deciding whether the denominator is the max entry or the sum (which changes what the bar means) and whether ranking is pre-sorted in a useMemo or delegated to a sortable table.

situations.name: Cost and burn-down
situations.definition: A developer needs spend broken down by source plus a projection of when a budget runs out.
situations.note: 'Spend' has multiple ledgers (companion_turn vs dev_llm_spend, per an audit comment) and burn-down needs a rate x remaining-budget projection that is fabricated when budget is unset; compositeHealthScore's comment documents a non-monotonic curve where OVERSPENDING once raised the health score.

situations.name: Event chain timeline
situations.definition: A developer needs a vertical narrative of related events with a connecting spine.
situations.note: Each timeline has a different ordering key (semantic phase order vs signed offset-seconds vs enum index) and a different spine geometry (CSS pseudo-line vs absolute div vs connector segments), so nothing shares.

situations.name: Trace waterfall viewer
situations.definition: A developer needs nested spans rendered as a collapsible duration waterfall.
situations.note: Shares buildSpanTree/flattenTree/getSpanConfig with the agents slice; the hard parts are that collapsed-ancestor visibility is a tree query executed on a flat list (O(n·depth) per render) and duration bars need a min-width floor or sub-ms spans vanish.

situations.name: Log tail viewer
situations.definition: A developer needs to display raw log or audit text, possibly streaming, with sensible scroll behaviour.
situations.note: Three <pre>-based viewers with different max-heights and no shared component; tail behaviour (stick-to-bottom vs preserve-scroll), virtualization and wrap handling each differ, and CrashLogsSection has to dedupe across three sources (Rust files, SQLite, localStorage).

situations.name: Machine-decision provenance
situations.definition: A developer needs to mark that an item was resolved or diagnosed by the system rather than a human.
situations.note: Provenance is a backend fact only one of four streams models as data — reviewHelpers detects auto-resolution by running REGEXES over free-text reviewer_notes because no column exists, which its own 14-line comment justifies.

situations.name: Node-link graph canvas
situations.definition: A developer needs a pannable, zoomable node-and-edge visualization of a knowledge or pattern graph.
situations.note: useGraphCanvas is a well-documented library-free camera (single <g transform>, cursor-anchored zoom, LOD helpers) with 3 consumers inside sub_patterns and zero outside — MemoriesPageGraph hand-rolls a static SVG cluster layout with no pan/zoom at all.

situations.name: Model-composed widget surface
situations.definition: A developer needs to render a dashboard whose layout and content an LLM emitted at runtime.
situations.note: 36 widget kinds behind one registry lookup with a matching Rust sanitizer validating kind, action-kind, and action-target legality per widget — the canonical answer exists, but adding a kind means editing a React registry, a Rust allowlist and Athena's constitution in lockstep, and nothing enforces that triple.

situations.name: LLM output fallback chain
situations.definition: A developer needs a surface that degrades from model-composed to deterministic to honest-quiet when generation fails or has nothing to say.
situations.note: The briefing gets it right — a delta gate skips the LLM call entirely when nothing happened, then compose, then deterministic fallback, then quiet — but nothing generalizes the pattern, so other Athena-composed surfaces re-derive their own degradation ladders.

situations.name: Session delta digest
situations.definition: A developer needs a 'here is what happened while you were away' summary anchored on a last-seen watermark.
situations.note: The subtle part is watermark ownership — the briefing must freeze the anchor during first render because a child heartbeat effect advances the stored value before any parent effect runs; libraryPulse solves the same window-digest shape independently and adds the rule that a digest is a projection, never stored.

situations.name: Adoption checklist probes
situations.definition: A developer needs a setup or feature-discovery checklist whose completion reflects the user's real data, not just clicks.
situations.note: powerMoves has the honest answer — an optional detect() probe against real data with a documented one-cheap-IPC budget, falling back to 'tried' — but the stepper and nav cards use unrelated completion models, so the same feature can read done in one surface and untouched in another.

situations.name: Destructive action confirmation
situations.definition: A developer needs a guard before delete, delete-all, or a sweep that cannot be undone.
situations.note: Two idioms coexist by intent — a modal ConfirmDialog for delete-all and an inline click-twice-within-3s for per-row delete — but the inline one is copy-pasted with its own timer cleanup twice, and nothing says which weight of action deserves which.

situations.name: Maintenance affordances
situations.definition: A developer needs dev-seed, garbage-collect and delete-all controls attached to a data surface.
situations.note: The `{import.meta.env.DEV && <button …amber-500/10…>}` seed block is byte-comparable across three files; only the ConfirmDialog shell is shared because each is a distinct per-table backend command, and one surface (incidents) has none of them at all.

situations.name: Threshold rule engine
situations.definition: A developer needs named thresholds that turn raw metrics into advice, alerts or badges.
situations.note: fleetOptimizer is the best-documented instance (7 named constants each with a rationale, including a recency bound added after weeks-old spikes rendered as current criticals), but every other engine scatters unnamed magic numbers and none are user-tunable the way alert rules are.

situations.name: Virtualized list
situations.definition: A developer needs a long list to render only visible rows while keeping grouping and entrance animation intact.
situations.note: Two primitives (GroupedVirtualList vs useVirtualList) plus UnifiedTable's own path; the friction is that virtualization fights the reveal cascade — every consumer hand-computes a reveal `order` offset from the virtual index.

situations.name: Attention badge registry
situations.definition: A developer needs the count of things needing attention in a domain, consistent across sidebar, tabs and dashboards.
situations.note: The template worth citing — a scoped registry with a count(state) selector per domain, written specifically because each surface used to reach into the store independently and drift; this is what the metric-identity registry should grow into.

situations.name: Route chunk prefetch
situations.definition: A developer needs lazily-loaded routes and widgets to be warm before the user navigates.
situations.note: Settled: lazyRetry everywhere, memoized prefetchers with failure-resets-the-cache, requestIdleCallback with a setTimeout fallback, and DeferUntilIdle for below-fold widgets.

situations.name: Long-running job progress
situations.definition: A developer needs to show a multi-minute backend job advancing, and reconcile its result when it lands.
situations.note: Four jobs, four polling loops, four progress vocabularies (percent, phase string, stream overlay, in-progress badge) — and no shared notion of what happens if the app is closed mid-job.

situations.name: Data table
situations.definition: A developer needs a sortable, resizable, filterable table of backend rows.
situations.note: DOCUMENTED ELSEWHERE — listed for recurrence only. Four column systems in this slice because UnifiedTable is grid-based with a width DSL, so a 9-column comparison matrix and a keyboard-navigable listbox both bail out and re-implement the header.

situations.name: Detail modal
situations.definition: A developer needs a modal presenting one record in depth with actions.
situations.note: DOCUMENTED ELSEWHERE — listed for recurrence only. Enforced by the custom/enforce-base-modal lint rule so the shell is uniform; the unsolved parts (queue-walking, keyboard arbitration) are catalogued separately above.

situations.name: Page loading choreography
situations.definition: A developer needs a route or panel to go from cold to painted without blank gaps, skeleton blinks or re-ghosting.
situations.note: DOCUMENTED ELSEWHERE — listed for recurrence only. The five laws are written down and broadly followed; residual divergence lives in the ghost-row and reveal-order conventions catalogued separately.
